profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.profile: This is the kind of file that makes stat nerds squint: the tee has been doing respectable work while the approach play keeps face-planting into a cactus. That combo can still cash checks in this league when the short game and putter decide to stop being strangers, which is exactly why the results have bounced around like a pinball machine. There’s enough pop to suggest the ceiling is real, but the floor is still held together with duct tape, one ugly miss, and a prayer.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: This dude is basically an argument for letting the irons swing the whole bag. The profile is built on loud tee shots, a nasty pile of birdies, and enough all-around juice to keep him near the top even when one part of the game gets weird for a round. The only real complaint is that the card can get messy when the driver starts freelancing, but that’s nitpicking on a file that mostly says: hit it, find it, hit it close, collect the trophy like it was inevitable.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.tagline: Short-game arson with a safety plan
profiles.profile: Matt is the league’s weird little alchemy experiment: the ball-striking is solid, the scoring clubs are usually fine, and then the wedges and putter occasionally show up like they’ve been bribed. The upside is obvious because the scoring ceiling is real when the short game wakes up, and he’s got enough gear to survive the off days without completely eating dirt. Not flashy. Not clean. Just annoyingly good at hanging around until the other guys explode first.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.profile: Keith keeps showing up like a guy who believes proximity is a personality trait. The irons are doing the heavy lifting, the putter is usually tagging along, and the whole thing has enough tee-to-green muscle to make him a constant problem. But there’s also a faint smell of grease on the file: when the edges get sloppy, the round can get noisy fast. Still, this is a seriously stout profile with more “make your life miserable” than “pray for survival.”

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.tagline: Approach god, putter with trust issues
profiles.profile: BigTime’s card is the golf equivalent of a guy who can thread a needle with a chainsaw. The approach play is ridiculous enough to keep the ceiling sky-high, but the tee can drift into nonsense and the putter has a habit of borrowing trouble. That’s why the results can look cleaner or messier than they should: the middle of the bag is doing heavy adult supervision while the rest of it occasionally wanders into traffic. Dangerous, volatile, and still annoyingly hard to ignore.

profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: The name is not a bit; it’s a scouting report. This file is a full-body stress test, with almost everything pointing the wrong direction and the scoring number getting dragged behind the cart like a broken bumper. The short game has been especially mean, but the larger problem is that nothing here is stable enough to build a real round on. When the best thing you can say is “well, it didn’t explode quite as badly this time,” the golf is doing its own roast.
